title: Rollback Reason Explorer and Annotated Canary Timeline
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Overview: Design an interactive panel inside the Private Console that helps operators quickly understand why a deployment was rolled back and where a canary failed. The feature combines a timeline that annotates canary traffic slices with per-step regression signals, and an explainer surface that maps failure reasons to recommended remediation actions (config change, infra scaling, or model variant fallback).

Goals:
- Reduce mean time to remediation for Private deployments by surfacing compact root-cause signals alongside rollout history.
- Make rollback decisions auditable: capture operator notes and automatically link the rollback to metrics/trace snapshots.
- Provide safe next-step suggestions with confidence scores so SREs can act faster without hunting across dashboards.

Scope: Focused on Private/VPC deployments only (first iteration). Integrates with existing telemetry: per-tenant latency percentiles, error rate, token cost anomalies, and model quality regression alerts (from Optimize). Does not include automatic rollback execution (engineering scope).

Design artifact links:
- Figma: https://redwood.design/figma/rollback-explorer-v1 (prototype v1, annotated)
- Miro: https://redwood.design/miro/rollback-workflow-board (stakeholder mapping, persona flows)
- Example metrics snapshot (APM): https://grafana.internal/board/rollouts/tenant-3011
- Mock data CSV used for prototype: gs://redwood-protos/rollback-explorer/mock-data-2026-02.csv

Key screens/components:
1) Canary Timeline (primary): horizontal timebar with shards (canary slices) and inline annotations: metric deltas, triggered alerts, top-3 contributing traces. Hover expands a compact trace summary.
2) Rollback Reason Card (right rail): natural-language summary generated from detected signals (e.g., "latency spike associated with KV-cache eviction during sequence-length > 1024"), confidence score, evidence links.
3) Suggested Remediations (actionables): prioritized suggestions with estimated impact and quick links to create an ops task or open a PR.
4) Audit Trail Composer: textarea for operator notes + auto-attached evidence (links to the exact traces/metrics used).

Design decisions / trade-offs documented during prototyping:
- Natural-language summary generation: we experimented with both short templated sentences and an LLM-generated paragraph. Chose templated first-pass to keep explanations deterministic and auditable.
- Evidence granularity: showing full traces vs. compact summaries. Opted for compact summaries by default with a single-click expand to full trace in APM to avoid cognitive overload.
- Inline remediation buttons: considered immediate runnable runbooks. For 1.0 we surface suggested actions with one-click to create issues/PRs; full playbook execution deferred to later.

Review feedback (chronological):
- 2026-02-25 (PM review - Elena Rossi): "Love the quick links to PRs and issues; ensure remediation estimates include cost deltas for Private capacity changes." -> added estimated cost delta field to Suggested Remediations.
- 2026-03-02 (Eng review - Mateo Silva): "Timeline looks dense at 24h view; we need aggregation thresholds and a compact mode for long windows." -> added aggregation rules and compact/expanded toggle in prototype.
- 2026-03-05 (Security - Priya Kapoor): "Audit trail must redact tenant PII by default and obtain an explicit operator confirmation if copying traces outside of the VPC console." -> added redaction reminder and CTA gating copy/share actions.
- 2026-03-08 (Design critique - Maya Ortiz): "Improve affordance for operator notes; allow attaching a snapshot version so notes link to immutable evidence." -> added snapshot creation CTA to Audit Trail Composer.

Accessibility & localization notes:
- Color choices follow our contrast tokens; rollback severity uses both color and icon + text so colorblind users can parse severity.
- Text in Rollback Reason Card limited to 280 characters by default with 'read more' for long explanations to simplify localization effort for 1.0.

Acceptance criteria (must be validated in handoff):
- Prototype shows a timeline with at least 3 annotation types and a working hover-to-expand trace summary.
- Rollback Reason Card populates from mock signals and displays confidence and 2 evidence links.
- Suggested Remediations list includes estimated latency impact and estimated cost delta.
- Audit Trail Composer creates a saved snapshot id that engineers can consume (mocked) and stores operator note text.

Next steps / Execution plan:
- (Design) Finalize responsive layouts for 1280px and 1600px canvases and hand off component specs (tokens, spacing, copy). Target: 2026-03-14 (Riya).
- (Eng) ENG-2119 to provide an API for snapshot creation and evidence links. Blocker until a read-only snapshot API exists.
- (Eng) ENG-2230 to add an event stream for canary slice metadata to power the timeline.
- (PM) PM to align on priority signals to show for 1.0: latency spike, error-rate jump, model-quality eval regression, token-cost anomaly.

Open questions and risks:
- Will teams accept templated NLG summaries or will they expect freeform LLM explanations? Risk: expectations gap might cause mistrust. Mitigation: include an "explainability" toggle in later cycles that surfaces how the summary was constructed.
- Snapshot retention policy: storing many snapshots may increase storage costs for Private deployments. PM to propose retention defaults and opt-in longer retention for large customers.

Stakeholders / reviewers: ["Elena Rossi (PM)", "Mateo Silva (ENG)", "Priya Kapoor (Security)", "Maya Ortiz (Design)", "Samir Gupta (SRE)"]

Notes from prototype user session (2026-03-09):
- Senior SRE tested with a staged rollback; they used the suggested remediation to open a quick-scaling PR and marked the rollback reason as "KV-cache pressure". They reported a 40% faster triage time vs the baseline flow.

Files to hand off in this ticket:
- designs: https://redwood.design/figma/rollback-explorer-v1
- prototype demo video: https://drive.redwood/videos/rollback-explorer-demo-2026-03-09.mp4
- handoff checklist: https://confluence.redwood/PrivateConsole/RollbackExplorer/HandoffChecklist

Owner notes: I iterated on edge cases where multiple signals conflict (e.g., cost anomaly concurrent with latency drop). The prototype shows a prioritized list and marks lower-confidence signals as "observational". We should productize a small taxonomy of rollback reasons (infra, model, config, networking) during implementation to keep UI stable across iterations.
